\paragraph{First measurement with the rev-2 channel in the loop.} The
cyclic-voltammetry test is the potentiostat bench of Section~\ref{ss:pixel} with
the linear cell swapped for the nonlinear one and nothing else changed: ideal
\(R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}\), \(C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{0.2}{\micro\farad}\),
\(R_u = R_{\mathrm{ce}} = \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}\), electrode at
\(E^{0\prime} = \SI{0.3}{\volt}\), \SI{1}{\milli\mole\per\litre},
\(k^0 = \SI{0.1}{\centi\metre\per\second}\), commanded over a
\SIrange{0.75}{1.75}{\volt} triangle at \SI{2}{\volt\per\second}, typical
process, \SI{37}{\celsius} for silicon and electrode alike.

The peak measures \SI{8.666}{\micro\ampere} against \SI{8.74}{\micro\ampere}
predicted (\SI{8.34}{\micro\ampere} Randles--\v{S}ev\v{c}\'ik plus
\SI{0.40}{\micro\ampere} of \(C_{\mathrm{dl}}\,\mathrm{d}v/\mathrm{d}t\)),
\SI{-0.8}{\percent}: the nonlinearity survives the loop rather than being
reshaped by it. Read as \(i_{\mathrm{we}} = (v_{\mathrm{out}} -
V_{\mathrm{CM}})/R_f\), the peak moves the output \SI{0.30}{\volt} from
\(V_{\mathrm{CM}} = \SI{1.25}{\volt}\), \SI{38}{\percent} of the
\(\pm\SI{0.80}{\volt}\) window, so the sweep is unclipped. The four wound-panel
analytes run as corners on the same test (Figure~\ref{fig:electrode-panel}).

\paragraph{What these numbers do not cover.}
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item Nominal transients only: one process point, one temperature, no corner
    set and no Monte Carlo. The analyte corners vary electrode parameters alone.
  \item A Verilog-A element carries no mismatch statistics, so every Monte Carlo
    \(\sigma\) in this chapter holds the electrode nominal and reports circuit
    variation only.
  \item Table~\ref{tab:electrode-peaks} runs at \SI{25}{\celsius}; the in-loop
    run is the only \SI{37}{\celsius} result. \texttt{Temp} is a plain model
    parameter, so a new bench must set it explicitly or the kinetics silently
    revert to \SI{25}{\celsius}. \(D\) is held at its \SI{25}{\celsius} value throughout, so the
    \(\sim\)30\,\% rise in a real aqueous \(D\) over \SIrange{25}{37}{\celsius}
    is not modelled.
  \item Randles--\v{S}ev\v{c}\'ik assumes semi-infinite diffusion; the model
    pins bulk at \(\delta = \SI{1.79}{\milli\metre}\). That holds by
    \(16\times\) at \SI{50}{\milli\volt\per\second} (\(\sqrt{Dt} =
    \SI{0.11}{\milli\metre}\)) but not for a thin unstirred
    film, for which a \SI{93}{\micro\metre} variant attenuates the reverse peak
    to \(0.65\) of the forward. Quote \(\delta\) with any peak from this model.
  \item \(k^0\) shapes the peak but neither identifies nor quantifies an
    analyte, and it is the least-supported parameter: no rate constant on carbon
    is published for these four markers, so the values in use are fitted to a
    measured \(\Delta E_p\). A gap in the literature, not the model.
\end{itemize}
